def transform(grid):
    from collections import Counter, deque
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0])
    bg=Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    # Find large monochrome rectangular fields, ignoring small marker interruptions.
    comps=[]; seen=set()
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            col=grid[r][c]
            if col==bg or (r,c) in seen: continue
            q=deque([(r,c)]); seen.add((r,c)); cells=[]
            while q:
                y,x=q.popleft(); cells.append((y,x))
                for yy,xx in ((y-1,x),(y+1,x),(y,x-1),(y,x+1)):
                    if 0<=yy<h and 0<=xx<w and (yy,xx) not in seen and grid[yy][xx]==col:
                        seen.add((yy,xx));q.append((yy,xx))
            if len(cells)>=4:
                rs=[y for y,x in cells]; cs=[x for y,x in cells]
                comps.append((col,min(rs),max(rs),min(cs),max(cs),len(cells)))
    # Major object color is the one with most cells (holes/noisy marker cells ignored).
    color_counts=Counter()
    for col,r0,r1,c0,c1,n in comps: color_counts[col]+=n
    main=max(color_counts,key=color_counts.get)
    out=[[bg]*w for _ in range(h)]
    # Preserve and fill the bounding rectangles of main-color objects; discard all markers.
    for col,r0,r1,c0,c1,n in comps:
        if col==main:
            for r in range(r0,r1+1):
                for c in range(c0,c1+1): out[r][c]=main
    return out
